structured_extraction.program_audience: New and expanding businesses.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: You can use funds to buy or improve real estate, purchase equipment, or for working capital related to the project.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must be a new or expanding business located in Queen Anne's County.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: The Economic Development Commission reviews funding requests. The County Commissioners authorize the disbursement of funds. Contact the agency to check for funding availability.

structured_extraction.program_description: Queen Anne's County offers a property tax credit to businesses that improve their property and create new jobs. The business must operate outside the county's Enterprise Zone.
structured_extraction.agency: Queen Anne's County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county provides a four-year tax credit on the increased value of the improved property. The credit is 80% in the first year, 60% in the second year, 40% in the third year, and 20% in the fourth year. The County Commissioners award the tax credit at their discretion.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Businesses in Queen Anne's County.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds must support real property improvements.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The business must be located in Queen Anne's County but outside of the Enterprise Zone.
requirements_list: Invest $25,000 or more in real property improvements.
Create at least 12 new full-time jobs within two years.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, download and complete the application form.

structured_extraction.program_description: Queen Anne’s County Economic & Tourism Development and the Upper Shore Regional Council offer grants to local agricultural businesses. The funds help businesses expand, diversify, improve marketing, complete capital projects, or conduct research.
structured_extraction.agency: Queen Anne’s County Economic & Tourism Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers competitive, cost-reimbursable grants from $2,500 to $10,000. A total of about $64,000 is available for fiscal year 2025.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Agricultural businesses
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: You can use grant funds for strategic marketing, technology innovation, climate resiliency projects, capital improvements, research projects, animal welfare improvements, and agritourism projects.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Applicants must operate an agricultural business in Queen Anne’s County, MD.
requirements_list: Must be actively engaged in the farming community.
Submit a project budget.
Provide documentation to support the financial request (e.g., quotes, receipts, invoices).
Submit Articles of Incorporation/Organization/Formation, Bylaws, and/or Operating Agreement, as applicable.
Grantees must complete a final grant report by June 15, 2025.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, submit a complete online application with all required documents by the deadline. A committee then reviews the applications in February 2025. The agency notifies applicants about funding decisions by email.

program_name: New and Expanding Business Tax Credit

structured_extraction.program_name: New and Expanding Business Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: St. Mary's County offers tax credits to support private businesses. The program helps companies that create jobs in targeted industries, locations, or underserved areas within the county.
structured_extraction.agency: Commissioners of St. Mary's County
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The county provides property tax credits based on job creation. Creating 10 to 15 jobs earns a $5,000 credit each year for five years. Creating 16 to 25 jobs provides an $8,000 credit each year for eight years. Creating 26 or more jobs offers a $10,000 credit each year for ten years. If a project includes new capital investment, the business also gets a 50% reduction on county property taxes for the new investment. The length of this extra credit depends on the number of jobs created.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for private businesses starting or growing in St. Mary's County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is available across St. Mary's County. It may focus on specific locations or markets that need more business activity.
requirements_list: Must be a private venture
Must result in job growth in St. Mary's County
Businesses creating 10 or more jobs are eligible for tiered credit amounts
Projects with new capital investment receive an additional property tax credit
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: To apply, a business must first submit the New and Expanding Business (NEXB) application. The Commissioners of St. Mary's County review the application and decide whether to approve the incentive. Submitting an application does not guarantee an award.

program_name: St. Mary’s County Facade and Streetscape Improvement Program

structured_extraction.program_name: St. Mary’s County Façade and Streetscape Improvement Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps business and property owners improve their buildings in certain areas. The program provides money back for projects that fix up building fronts and nearby sidewalks. The goal is to make these areas look better, encourage more investment, and improve safety.
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program pays back 50% of a project's cost. The maximum amount you can receive is $6,000.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Commercial property owners and business owners in specific parts of Lexington Park and Charlotte Hall.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: You can use funds to improve the outside of buildings. This includes storefronts and sidewalks next to the property.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Projects must be in the 'Downtown' and 'Great Mills Corridor' areas of Lexington Park, as defined by the Lexington Park Master Plan. Projects can also be in the designated Sustainable Communities area of Charlotte Hall.
requirements_list: Property must be located within the designated grant area.
Proposed work must be an eligible project.
Cost estimates must come from licensed and insured contractors.
Limited to one application per address per calendar year.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, confirm your property is in an eligible location and your project qualifies. Next, get cost estimates from licensed contractors. Then, gather all required documents. Finally, submit the complete application online in a single session, as you cannot save it and return later.

program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit

structured_extraction.program_name: Job Creation and Capital Investment Real Property Tax Credit
structured_extraction.program_description: This program provides a real property tax credit to businesses. It helps attract new companies and supports existing companies that expand in Washington County.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program offers a tax credit on the increased value of a business's real property after it expands or builds a new facility. The credit amount and duration depend on the project tier. Tier 1 provides credits up to 52% for six years. Tier 2 provides credits up to 30% for six years. Tier 3 provides credits up to 100% for fifteen years for major investments.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Rolling, before project construction is complete
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program helps new and existing businesses that locate or expand in Washington County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The business property must be located in a Priority Funding Area in Washington County. Businesses located in an Enterprise Zone are not eligible for this program.
requirements_list: Must be located in a Priority Funding Area.
Cannot be located in an Enterprise Zone.
Submit an application before construction is complete.
Tier 1 (Existing Business): Expand by at least 1,500 sq. ft. and create at least 1 new full-time job paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage.
Tier 2 (New Business): Obtain at least 2,500 sq. ft. of space and create at least 5 new full-time jobs paying at least 150% of the federal minimum wage.
Tier 3 (New or Existing Business): Invest at least $10,000,000 in capital improvements and create at least 100 new full-time jobs.
Must provide annual employment reports to maintain the credit.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, a business must notify the county of its intent to apply for the credit. Then, it submits an application to the Department of Business Development before finishing construction. The department will certify the business if it is eligible. After certification and project completion, the business must create the required number of new jobs. The business must submit yearly reports on employment to maintain the credit.

program_name: High Performance Commercial Building Tax Incentive Program

structured_extraction.program_name: High Performance Commercial Building Tax Incentive Program
structured_extraction.program_description: This program gives property tax credits to owners of commercial buildings in Washington County. Owners receive the credit for constructing or renovating buildings to meet high energy and environmental standards. To qualify, buildings must earn a Silver, Gold, or Platinum rating from the Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design (LEED) system.
structured_extraction.agency: Washington County Department of Business Development
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides a tax credit for three years. The credit applies to the increased property value after new construction or renovation. The amount is 20% of the increase for a LEED Silver rating, 25% for Gold, and 30% for Platinum.
structured_extraction.application_deadline_string: Apply within 1 year after the building is certified as a “high performance building”.
structured_extraction.program_audience: Owners of commercial buildings in Washington County.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: The program is for commercial properties located in Washington County.
requirements_list: The property must be a commercial building.
The building must achieve a LEED Silver, Gold, or Platinum rating.
The application must be submitted within one year of the building receiving its LEED certification.
The building must maintain its certification level for the three-year credit period.
Applicants must submit an annual letter of compliance.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, the building owner submits a complete application form. They must include a copy of their LEED certification request. After the project is finished, the owner must provide a use and occupancy certificate and proof of the final LEED certification. The Department of Business Development then reviews the materials to approve the tax credit.

structured_extraction.program_description: The Tri-County Council for Western Maryland offers this loan program to help businesses in Allegany, Garrett, and Washington counties. The program provides gap financing, which means it partners with banks to fund the part of a project that a primary lender cannot cover. The main goal is to create or keep jobs in the region.
structured_extraction.agency: Tri-County Council for Western Maryland
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides loans from $10,000 to $400,000. It offers this financing as gap funding, meaning a bank or other private lender must fund at least 50% of the project. The interest rates connect to the prime interest rate. Loan terms are up to 5 years for working capital and up to 15 years for fixed assets like real estate.
structured_extraction.program_audience: This program is for businesses, including corporations, partnerships, and sole proprietorships. The business must be in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County. It is for businesses that cannot get all their needed funding from traditional lenders.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: You can use funds for business acquisition and expansion. You can also use them for land and building costs, buying machinery and equipment, start-up costs, and working capital.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must be located in Allegany, Garrett, or Washington County to be eligible.
requirements_list: A business plan is required.
A private lender must fund at least 50% of the total project cost.
Applicant must provide a denial letter from the primary lender for 100% of the project, along with their approval to finance a majority of the project.
One job must be created or retained for every $30,000 borrowed within the first 36 months of the loan.
A minimum equity injection of 10% is generally required for start-up businesses.
Personal guaranties of the debt are required from all owners with 20% or greater interest.
Applicants must provide a completed personal financial statement and 3 years of both business and personal tax returns.
A $250 non-refundable application fee is required.
Approved borrowers are assessed a 1.5% loan origination fee at closing.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: First, create a business plan and determine your funding needs. Second, apply for a loan from a private bank to determine how much they will finance. Third, complete the program's application form and submit it with the required documents and application fee.

structured_extraction.program_description: This program helps new and existing agriculture and resource-based businesses grow in Wicomico County. It is a partnership between Wicomico County, PNC Bank, and the Maryland Agricultural & Resource Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO).
structured_extraction.agency: Salisbury-Wicomico Economic Development (SWED)
structured_extraction.assistance_description: The program provides grant funds to support projects. It operates as a cost-share program.
structured_extraction.program_audience: The program supports new and existing for-profit businesses in agriculture and resource-based industries.
structured_extraction.use_of_funds: Funds can be used for projects that support Wicomico County’s farming, forestry, or seafood industries. This includes businesses involved in agritourism or the production, packaging, processing, or marketing of agricultural products.
structured_extraction.geographic_eligibility: Businesses must have their headquarters and main operations in Wicomico County.
requirements_list: The applicant must contribute at least 50% of the total project cost.
The business must be registered and in good standing with the State of Maryland and Wicomico County.
The project must help Wicomico County's farming, forestry, or seafood industries.
Businesses that package, process, or market agricultural products are also eligible.
structured_extraction.application_process_overview: Applicants submit an application to Salisbury-Wicomico Economic Development (SWED). SWED then submits the application to the Maryland Agricultural & Resource Based Industry Development Corporation (MARBIDCO). Both SWED and MARBIDCO must approve the application.
